question: Two engineers check the same drawing independently and both approve it. Is the drawing twice as safe?
options: Only if their mistakes are unrelated
answer: Two checks only multiply if they can fail for different reasons. Trained the same way, working from the same brief, they tend to miss the same things — which is why serious systems try to make their checks disagree.
move: Two checks that would fail together are one check.
trap: Adding checks feels like multiplying safety.
